text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- National Assembly to debate Social Security finances today.
-- Computer services firms Axime and Sligos consider industrial alliance.

-- Jean-Charles Naouri, chairman of Euris which is a majority shareholder in Casino and Moulinex, says he supports the Moulinex restructuring plan and does not rule out possibility of strategic alliances for Casino.
-- Canal Plus subscriber-TV channel signs long- term alliance with MCA film studios.
-- Air France chairman Christian Blanc says airline and its shareholders may consider bidding for AOM airline, up for sale by structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets.
-- Societe Generale considers selling assets and real-estate property.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES

-- Finance Ministry expected to gain some four billion francs from reshuffling withdrawal conditions for subscribers of PEP housing savings plans, a measure initially designed to boost consumption by increasing purchasing power of low-income families.
-- Lagardere shares drop 6.9 percent at Paris bourse after widespread criticism on the conditions of its offer on Thomson.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis reaffirms in an interview that France needs to straighten its public finances even if it were not not for Maastricht treaty criteria, adds that the euro will be an instrument of monetary stability, helping economic exchanges and employment.
-- Political criticism of government's choice of Lagardere to take over Thomson may lead privatisation committee to question this choice, finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- 72 percent of the French criticise sale of Thomson, a 70-billion-turnover group employing 9,600 workers for one symbolic franc, survey shows.
-- Health spending decreased o.4 percent in September, increasing chances that a 2.1 percent yearly increase target set for 1996 may be met.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Paris City Council to probe allegations that some city-owned property currently up for sale was seized from Jews deported during World War Two.
